Assistant
Roofing worksheet: SC09 room (read-only, draft)

First-course-full rule. The first course lays the full sheet length L with no end-lap deduction, because nothing precedes it. Each later course starts E below the previous course end, so it adds L-E. Using ceil(R/(L-E)) wrongly subtracts a phantom end lap from the first course.

Columns, courses, sheets, ordered linear metres.

Columns = ceil(W/C) = ceil(8/0.8) = 10.
Courses = 1 when 0 < R ≤ L; otherwise 1 + ceil((R-L)/(L-E)).
Sheets = columns × courses.
Ordered linear metres = sheets × L.

Side lap is already folded into the effective cover C (0.8 m). Do not deduct it a second time as a width or column adjustment.

Course-count boundaries (L = 5 m, E = 0.2 m, L-E = 4.8 m).

R = 5.0 m: R ≤ L, courses = 1; sheets = 10; ordered linear metres = 50.
R just above 5.0 m: courses = 2; sheets = 20; ordered linear metres = 100.
R = 9.8 m: courses = 1 + ceil(4.8/4.8) = 2 (lower count kept at the exact coverage boundary); sheets = 20; ordered linear metres = 100.
R just above 9.8 m: courses = 3; sheets = 30; ordered linear metres = 150.

Arithmetic is a worksheet convention only. Figures are draft and verifiedQuoteEligible=false.

Developer review

Outcome: explained the first-course-full rule, all four run boundaries, and columns/courses/sheets/ordered linear metres using only the supplied synthetic inputs.
Friction: none notable; kept each metric on its own line and avoided any combined rollup.

Assistant
QS synthetic export: SC09 room (read-only, draft)

Whole-draft vs filtered totals. Whole-draft totals include every leaf in the export, including B (unassigned, m², unverified) and D (assigned to Building, m², inferred). A subtree rollup includes only items assigned directly to that node or to its descendants, so A and C enter the Walls rollup; D enters the Building rollup; B enters neither parent.

Do not sum parent + child. Walls inclusive (A + C) and Building inclusive (D + Walls inclusive) overlap on C and on A. Adding them double-counts Walls leaves. A filtered parent total already contains its children.

Flat vs hierarchical CSV.

Flat item-only CSV: rows are items only. Sum within each (unit, evidence class). Nothing else is a row.
Hierarchical CSV: rows are labelled SUMMARY_NODE or LEAF_ITEM. Sum each leaf once within its (unit, evidence class). Skip summary rows.

Wall-vs-Building rollups (separated by unit/evidence):

Walls m² unverified = 0.10 (A).
Walls lm sample = 3 (C).
Building m² inferred = 4.00 (D).
Unassigned m² unverified = 0.20 (B).

Apostrophe in `'=1+1`. A leading apostrophe forces text in the cell so a spreadsheet does not evaluate it; display depends on the importing app.

Developer review

Outcome: covered whole vs filtered, parent/child overlap, flat vs SUMMARY_NODE/LEAF_ITEM, every (unit, evidence) subtotal, and the apostrophe from supplied evidence.
Friction: none notable; kept each subtotal on its own line and avoided any cross-class combined figure.
Improvement: none specific to this response.
